newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Juppe says dollar chronically undervalued.
newsitem.headline: France's Juppe says dollar chronically undervalued.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe said on Monday the dollar was chronically undervalued.

"We will not give up repeating it -- there is a problem of chronic undervaluation of the dollar to which we will find a cure when we have the means with the creation of a single european currency and the euro," Juppe said.
Juppe told the Senate the move to monetary union had already won the credibility argument and that France was well on the road to this goal with a stable currency and low interest rates.

For the single currency to bear fruit, there had to be clear game rules between those who joined from the outset and those who did not, Juppe said, adding that these game rules should "protect us from the competitive devaluations" of the past.
"France has managed to get this idea accepted by its partners, which was not a foregone conclusion a few months back," he said.

"The second condition that will make the euro an advantage in international competition is that its parity with the major world currencies, and above all the dollar, be managed in line with economic reality," he said.
